source.title: RelP: Faithful and Efficient Circuit Discovery in Language Models via Relevance Patching
source.authors: F. Jafari; Oliver Eberle; Ashkan Khakzar; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study uses IOI as a benchmark to compare patching approximations, but it does not test the specified 26-head circuit or any of the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The IOI results measure how closely AtP and RelP component scores align with activation patching; they do not establish circuit membership, head roles, or circuit faithfulness, completeness, and minimality. The study also reports a separate Subject–Verb Agreement experiment, which is not about the claimed IOI circuit and is not recorded here.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI task (templates from Wang et al.) only as a benchmark for how well AtP and RelP approximate activation patching scores. It reports its own method's agreement with activation patching. It never identifies or evaluates the 26-head circuit, head classes, backup heads, or circuit faithfulness/completeness on IOI. This is T4 (uses as tool, reports own method performance) rather than cites_only/T6, since IOI prompts and the patching setup are actually used.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one fix. RelP aligns better with activation patching than AtP on IOI across models, though not universally: AtP is slightly higher for GPT-2 small attention outputs. RelP also matches IG faithfulness for sparse feature circuits (subject–verb agreement, Pythia-70M) at lower cost. The authors' own text inconsistently says RelP matches AtP faithfulness; they mean IG.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares RelP and AtP against activation patching as component-score approximations on IOI; it does not apply the original IOI circuit-discovery and evaluation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported PCCs vary by model and component type. No template-specific or prompt-distribution sensitivity analysis is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 8 models on 100 IOI prompt pairs, RelP's component scores correlate more with activation patching than AtP's. Example: GPT-2 large MLP outputs, 0.956 vs 0.006. Gains are smaller for attention outputs; GPT-2 small attention is AtP 0.979 vs RelP 0.962.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LRP-based relevance patching approximates activation patching on IOI more faithfully than gradient-based attribution patching, especially for residual stream and MLP outputs.

record.problems: The IOI comparison reports PCCs without uncertainty estimates. The authors note that their experiments use small- and medium-scale open-access models, predefined original–patch pairs, and single-token prediction metrics; their study does not directly evaluate the claimed circuit.
record.rows_left_out: The study's Subject–Verb Agreement feature-circuit results are outside the IOI claim and were left out. No IOI table rows were omitted.

untested.parts: 26 heads, 7 classes, and faithfulness/completeness/minimality of the GPT-2 small IOI circuit: not examined.
Backup name-mover heads and self-repair: not examined.
Same head classes in other models, sizes or checkpoints: not examined. IOI is run on eight models, but only patching-score correlations are reported.
Whether other methods recover the same IOI circuit: not examined. Agreement of component scores between AtP/RelP and activation patching is not circuit recovery.

Sensitivity of IOI circuit faithfulness/completeness to ablation, metric or distribution: not examined. Faithfulness/completeness is reported only for subject–verb agreement feature circuits in Pythia-70M.
IOI mechanism across name orders, templates or more names: not examined. Three ABBA-style templates are used, with no per-template analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche changed from cites_only/T6 to uses_without_test/T4, because IOI prompts and patching are actually used as a benchmark. The study makes no verdict-relevant IOI circuit claims. No uncertainty is reported on the PCCs.

versions.untested_parts: The 26 attention heads, seven classes, their roles, and the stated faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Backup heads and self-repair after ablating main name-mover heads.
Circuit reuse across models, sizes, checkpoints, and tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
Sensitivity of circuit faithfulness and completeness to ablation, metric, or prompt distribution, and how much behavior the circuit explains.
Whether the same circuit carries IOI across name orders, templates, or more names.

rows.check: All rows R01–R48 are the study's own method (RelP) compared with AtP, both measured against activation patching. They are method-comparison values, not results on the IOI circuit, and should be marked as such rather than as claim evidence. Links ['none'] and cannot_determine are correct.
